uncertainty: Pilot cell: seven Rust paths verified (hickory-proto, simple-dns, domain, dns-parser, dns-message-parser, rustdns, rsdns), ranked by crates.io recent_downloads (90 days). Remaining leads: dns-protocol (unresolved), packet-dissector-dns (unresolved), dns_parse (unresolved), dnsparse (unresolved). Excluded after checking: trust-dns-proto, mdns-sd (reasons in leads.json). Metric values are crates.io recent_downloads (90 days) from the snapshot; round 1 had recorded all-time downloads under that label, corrected in round 2. trust-dns-proto 0.23.2 (hickory-proto's previous crate name) passed the full gate but is excluded as a predecessor sharing most of the decoder code; its records are archived in trust-dns-proto-demoted.json. Rust AFL++ overlays are scoped to the parser crates (afl_instrumented_crates) because the summary encoder's random hashing made whole-binary maps unstable. Each verified path parses the two valid controls (a query and a response with compressed CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers) to the hand-written oracle summary, has library source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback that differs between the controls. Two valid controls do not establish EDNS0, DNSSEC, TXT, authority/additional or malformed-input behaviour. Package-level adoption metrics include non-DNS use, and the cell is not a definitive top ten.
